{"id":"fedistract-rr9g.4","title":"Create fedi-e2ee crate: encrypted direct messages","description":"End-to-end encrypted direct messages using DID key exchange. The most user-requested fediverse feature.

Backwards-compatible: DMs are sent as standard AP Direct messages with encrypted content. The 'content' field contains a human-readable fallback ('This message is encrypted. Your server does not support encrypted messages.'). The actual ciphertext is in a new 'encryptedContent' field that unaware servers store but can't read.

Crypto design:
1. Key agreement: Convert Ed25519 signing keys to X25519 for Diffie-Hellman
   (ed25519-dalek provides this via SigningKey::to_scalar())
2. Derive shared secret: X25519 ECDH between sender and recipient
3. KDF: HKDF-SHA256 to derive encryption key from shared secret
4. Encryption: XChaCha20-Poly1305 (AEAD, 192-bit nonce = safe with random nonces)
5. Encode: multibase base64url the ciphertext + nonce

Public API:
- encrypt_dm(plaintext: &str, sender_private: &[u8; 32], recipient_public: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<EncryptedMessage>
  Returns EncryptedMessage { ciphertext: String, nonce: String, sender_did: String }

- decrypt_dm(msg: &EncryptedMessage, recipient_private: &[u8; 32], sender_public: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<String>
  Returns plaintext.

- prepare_dm_note(note: &mut serde_json::Value, encrypted: &EncryptedMessage)
  Adds encryptedContent field to Note, replaces content with fallback text.

- extract_encrypted_content(note: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<EncryptedMessage>
  Extracts encryptedContent from received Note if present.

Key discovery: recipient's Ed25519 public key is in their actor document's DID or publicKey field. The did:key in alsoKnownAs contains the raw Ed25519 public key (multicodec-decoded). This is why the DID infiltration had to happen first.

Multi-recipient: for group DMs, encrypt separately for each recipient (one ciphertext per recipient, all in an array). This is how Signal/MLS work — no shared group key needed for small groups.

Deps: x25519-dalek, chacha20poly1305, hkdf, sha2, fedi-did, multibase, rand.

Security notes:
- Forward secrecy: NOT provided in this design (Ed25519 keys are long-lived). This is acceptable for the MVP because the alternative (no encryption at all) is worse. Double-ratchet (Signal protocol) can be added later.
- Nonce: 192-bit random (XChaCha20), safe to generate randomly without counter.
- Recipient key validation: verify recipient's public key is on the curve before ECDH.
- Zeroize: all intermediate key material (shared secret, derived key) must be zeroized after use.
- Metadata: server admins can still see who is messaging whom (envelope metadata). Only content is encrypted. This is inherent to AP's routing model.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"feature","owner":"mark@wolfssl.com","created_at":"2026-07-20T02:54:44.617441816Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-07-20T02:54:44.617441816Z","dependencies":[{"issue_id":"fedistract-rr9g.4","depends_on_id":"fedistract-rr9g","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-07-20T02:54:44.629189597Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
